([[Virginia Beach, Virginia]]) | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] / [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] | career_number=45 | draft_year = 2004 | career_start = 2004 | career_end = 2007 | years1=2004–2005 | team1=[[Great Lakes Storm]] | years2={{nbay|2004|end}}–{{nbay|2005|end}} | team2=[[New York Knicks]] | years3 = {{nbay|2006|full=yes}} | team3=[[San Antonio Spurs]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2007 NBA Finals|2007]]) * All-[[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] First Team (2005) * [[Continental Basketball Association Rookie of the Year Award|CBA Rookie of the Year]] (2005) * CBA All-Rookie Team (2005) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2003 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2003]]) * Second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2003) * [[Mississippi Mr. Basketball]] (2002) }} '''Jackie Butler''' (born March 10, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He attended [[McComb High School]] in [[McComb, Mississippi]], and transferred to Coastal Christian Academy in [[Virginia Beach, Virginia|Virginia Beach]] for his final high school season. Butler skipped college and declared for the 2004 NBA draft, but was not selected. He joined the [[Great Lakes Storm]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA), and won [[Continental Basketball Association Rookie of the Year Award|Rookie of the Year]] whilst also being named to the All-CBA First Team. Butler signed with the [[New York Knicks]] in February 2005. In July 2006, he signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], whom he won the [[2007 NBA Finals]] with. ==Early life== Butler was born in [[McComb, Mississippi]] and attended McComb High School and originally committed to play at [[Mississippi State University]] but failed to qualify academically. He enrolled at [[Laurinburg Institute]] in [[North Carolina]] for academic purposes but he departed after a reported altercation with a teammate.{{cite web |title=Grandmother Says Butler Didn’t Receive Money |url=https://www.enterprise-journal.com/sports/grandmother-says-butler-didnt-receive-money?e_term_id=20963 |website=Enterprise-Journal |access-date=December 25, 2022 |date=March 15, 2021}} He then transferred to Coastal Christian Academy [[University-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Virginia Beach, Virginia|Virginia Beach]].{{cite web |title=A Prep Player's Journey to Pros |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB111055760734577181 |website=Wall Street Journal |access-date=December 25, 2022 |date=March 14, 2005}} Although he wanted to sign with the [[University of Tennessee]] in 2004, he decided to declare for the [[2004 NBA draft]], the first player that year to do so.{{cite web|last=Monter|first=Chris|title=Jackie Butler is first early entry into NBA Draft|url=http://collegebasketballnews.scout.com/2/234047.html|work=CollegeBasketballNews.com|access-date=February 12, 2012|date=February 12, 2004|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070918180741/http://collegebasketballnews.scout.com/2/234047.html|archive-date=September 18, 2007}} ==Professional career== ===Great Lakers Storm (2004–2005)=== Butler went undrafted in the [[2004 NBA draft]] and signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] but was cut before the season began. Butler began the 2004–05 season with the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) where over 40 games with the [[Great Lakes Storm]] he averaged 18.1 points, 10.7 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Teenage Center Signs With the Knicks |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/02/28/sports/basketball/teenage-center-signs-with-the-knicks.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=September 16, 2020 |date=February 28, 2005}} He was named the [[Continental Basketball Association Rookie of the Year Award|CBA Rookie of the Year]] and selected to the All-CBA First Team.{{cite web |title=Jackie Butler minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-butlejac001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 23, 2021}} ===New York Knicks (2005–2006)=== On February 27, 2005, Butler signed with the [[New York Knicks]] for the rest of the [[2004–05 NBA season]], scoring ten points over three games. He later was drafted in the 2005 [[All-American Professional Basketball League|AAPBL]] draft. However, the league folded soon thereafter. When [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]] was hired as the [[New York Knicks]]' head coach, it was unclear what sort of role Butler would have. After the preseason, Brown publicly commented on how happy he was with Butler, and considered him his fourth rookie (after [[Channing Frye]], [[Nate Robinson]], and [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]]). After a rocky start, Butler was soon praised as being the Knicks' best center, with [[Eddy Curry]] and [[Jerome James]] having disappointing starts to their Knicks careers. For the [[2005–06 NBA season]] Butler played in 55 games averaging 13.5 minutes, 5.3 points (54.4% field goal accuracy) and 3.3 rebounds per game. He earned US$641,748 with the Knicks. ===San Antonio Spurs (2006–2007)=== In July 2006, Butler signed a three-year, US$7 million contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|last=Beck|first=Howard|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/07/20/sports/basketball/20knicks.html|title=Looking at Bottom Line, Knicks Let Butler Go|date=July 20, 2006}} He was considered a long-term project. Spurs coach [[Gregg Popovich]] said on October 26, 2006, "most of his playing time in the initial part of the season is going to be in practice, learning what a work ethic is day in and day out and what it takes to play at this level."{{cite web|last=Ludden|first=Johnny|url=http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA102706.01D.BKNspurs.butler.3086c0b.html|title=Butler finding right track with Spurs|work=San Antonio Express-News|date=October 26, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312223950/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA102706.01D.BKNspurs.butler.3086c0b.html|archive-date=March 12, 2008}} Butler never played with the Spurs during the [[2007 NBA playoffs|2007 NBA Playoffs]], but the Spurs won the [[2007 NBA Finals]].{{cite web|title=Jackie Butler bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jackie_butler/bio.html|publisher=NBA|access-date=February 12,
